puzzles.prompt: Largest economies by nominal GDP
puzzles.metric: Gross domestic product at current prices in US dollars, IMF projection for 2026
puzzles.ambiguity: Ranked by NOMINAL GDP. Measured at purchasing power parity the order differs sharply - China ranks first and India third.

puzzles.prompt: Highest mountains in the world
puzzles.metric: Elevation above sea level, in metres. Distinct peaks only, not subsidiary summits.
puzzles.ambiguity: Ranked by elevation above sea level. By prominence, or by height above base, a very different ten appears.

puzzles.prompt: Longest rivers in the world
puzzles.metric: Length in kilometres from the most distant headstream to the mouth, including named tributary systems
puzzles.ambiguity: Whether the Nile or the Amazon is longest is genuinely contested and turns on which Amazon headstream you accept. This puzzle follows Britannica in placing the Nile first.

puzzles.prompt: Most Super Bowl titles by franchise

puzzles.ambiguity: Several franchises are tied on wins, so the order within a tie is arbitrary; the ten clubs are what matters. NFL championships won before the Super Bowl era are not counted.

puzzles.prompt: Largest islands in the world
puzzles.metric: Island area in km². Continental landmasses are not counted as islands.
puzzles.ambiguity: Australia is excluded as a continental landmass rather than an island; including it would put it first by a wide margin.

puzzles.prompt: Largest deserts in the world
puzzles.metric: Desert area in km², where a desert is defined by low precipitation rather than by heat. Polar deserts count.
puzzles.ambiguity: Defining deserts by aridity rather than temperature puts the two polar deserts at the top. Lists that only count hot deserts begin with the Sahara and produce a different ten.

puzzles.prompt: Most abundant elements in Earth's crust
puzzles.metric: Share of the Earth's crust by mass, as a percentage.

source.name: CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics - abundance of elements

puzzles.ambiguity: By mass, and for the crust only. The Earth as a whole is mostly iron, and by number of atoms rather than mass the order shifts.

puzzles.prompt: Most valuable companies by market capitalisation
puzzles.metric: Market capitalisation in US dollars — share price times shares outstanding — for publicly listed companies.

confidence.note: The top eight are confirmed; the ninth and tenth places move week to week and are my best judgment at the as-of date.

puzzles.ambiguity: State-owned companies without a full public listing are ranked by estimated valuation, which some lists exclude entirely.

puzzles.prompt: Largest companies in the world by revenue
puzzles.metric: Annual revenue in US dollars, Fortune Global 500 methodology, which includes state-owned enterprises.

confidence.note: The top two and the presence of the US health and tech giants are confirmed. The Chinese state-owned entrants and the exact order below fifth are my best judgment — the published list ranks by revenue, not the market value most other rankings use.

puzzles.ambiguity: Ranking by revenue rather than profit or market value puts retailers and state energy firms far above more valuable technology companies.

puzzles.prompt: Most valuable brands in the world
puzzles.metric: Brand value in US dollars — what the name itself is worth, separate from the company's assets — by Interbrand methodology.

confidence.note: The leading names are stable year to year, but the order below fourth and the exact tenth place shift between annual reports and between rival methodologies.

puzzles.ambiguity: Brand valuation is a modelled estimate, and the major agencies publish materially different rankings from the same year.

puzzles.prompt: Biggest coffee-producing countries
puzzles.metric: Green coffee production by weight, in tonnes per year.

confidence.note: The top five are confirmed. Places six to ten are close together and reorder with the harvest, so their membership is my best judgment — Guatemala and Nicaragua are near misses.

source.name: OIV - State of the world vine and wine sector

confidence.note: The top four are firm. The rest swap places with the vintage — a bad harvest moves a country several spots — and the tenth place is my best judgment.

puzzles.prompt: Biggest cocoa-producing countries

confidence.note: The West African leaders are certain and dominate the total. The lower half is closely bunched and my best judgment.

puzzles.prompt: Tallest buildings in the world
puzzles.metric: Architectural height in metres, counting spires but not antennas, for completed buildings.

confidence.note: The top five are confirmed. The rest are from the standard CTBUH ordering and are tightly bunched — two of them are within two metres of each other.

puzzles.ambiguity: Counting spires but not antennas is what puts some towers above others; measured to the highest occupied floor, the order changes.

puzzles.prompt: Busiest airports in the world by passengers
puzzles.metric: Total passengers handled in a calendar year, arrivals plus departures plus transfers.

confidence.note: All ten are confirmed for the as-of year; one figure in the middle of the order is estimated from its neighbours.

puzzles.ambiguity: Ranked by total passengers, which counts transfers. By international passengers only, the Gulf and European hubs rise and the American ones fall away.

puzzles.prompt: Largest lakes in the world by area
puzzles.metric: Surface area in km².
puzzles.ambiguity: The largest is called a sea and is saline, but is landlocked and counted as a lake here. Two of the Great Lakes are hydrologically one body and are sometimes merged into a single entry, which would change the order.

puzzles.prompt: Brightest stars in the night sky
puzzles.metric: Apparent magnitude as seen from Earth, excluding the Sun. Lower magnitude means brighter.
puzzles.ambiguity: Apparent brightness from Earth, not actual luminosity — several of these only look bright because they are close. Multiple-star systems are ranked on their combined light.

puzzles.prompt: Most abundant gases in Earth's atmosphere
puzzles.metric: Share of dry air by volume, as a percentage.
puzzles.ambiguity: Measured for dry air. Water vapour varies from almost nothing to about 4% by volume and would rank third where it is abundant, so it is excluded by convention.
